pr_title: server: use max_allowed_packet to limit the packet size.
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #31422

Problem Summary:

The `max_allowed_packet` exists but did not work on previous versions.

### What is changed and how it works?

1. truncate the value of `max_allowed_packet` if it is not a multiple of 1024
2. report an error if the accumulated length of a packet is longer than `max_allowed_packet`

See https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/packet-too-large.html

issue_context.title: max_allowed_packet length is set to 1024 but its not working for string length.
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
set global max_allowed_packet=100;
set global net_buffer_length=100;  # change session
select @@net_buffer_length, @@max_allowed_packet;
SELECT length("") as len;

```
### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```sql
mysql> select @@net_buffer_length, @@max_allowed_packet;
+---------------------+----------------------+
| @@net_buffer_length | @@max_allowed_packet |
+---------------------+----------------------+
|                1024 |                 1024 |
+---------------------+----------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> SELECT length("") as len;
ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
```
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```sql
mysql> select @@net_buffer_length, @@max_allowed_packet;
+---------------------+----------------------+
| @@net_buffer_length | @@max_allowed_packet |
+---------------------+----------------------+
| 100                 |                 1024 |
+---------------------+----------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> SELECT length("") as len;
+------+
| len  |
+------+
| 1024 |
+------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

```
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
```sql
| Release Version: v5.5.0-alpha-21-g722303bca-dirty
Edition: Community
Git Commit Hash: 722303bca8d279ff7c9d87e942095d320499f47e
Git Branch: master
UTC Build Time: 2022-01-05 19:11:01
GoVersion: go1.16.9
Race Enabled: false
TiKV Min Version: v3.0.0-60965b006877ca7234adaced7890d7b029ed1306
Check Table Before Drop: false |

```
comments: Also notice the duplicate issue #32164 mentions that it causes TiDB to crash due to Out-Of-Memory!
Although assigned, it seems that this issue does not have any updates in a month, so I'd like to take a try.

review_comments:
Please add a test case for `set @@global.max_allowed_packet=0`(the result should be `1024`).

Also, I noticed that MySQL gives the following warning for `set @@global.max_allowed_packet=0`:

```
mysql> show warnings;
+---------+------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                                                                   |
+---------+------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Truncated incorrect max_allowed_packet value: '0'                                         |
| Warning | 1708 | The value of 'max_allowed_packet' should be no less than the value of 'net_buffer_length' |
+---------+------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
However, `net_buffer_length` is a no-op variable in TiDB, so I don't think this warning is necessary so we don't have to add the extra warning check for it. /cc @morgo
I agree it's not necessary to add the warning.

Some weird behavior I encountered:
```
tidb> set @@max_allowed_packet=0;
tidb> CREATE TABLE WALLET(user_id int, currency_id int, amount int, expiry_time DATETIME, is_lifetime int, pack_id int, sub_org_id int);
```
Then(see attached sql.txt):
```
tidb> source sql.txt
```
* MySQL:
```
mysql> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    15
Current database: *** NONE ***

ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
mysql> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    16
Current database: *** NONE ***

ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
```

This PR:
```
tidb> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    431
Current database: test

ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    433
Current database: test

ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
tidb> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    435
Current database: test

ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    437
Current database: test

ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
```
However, if I set a breakpoint right here, and 'continue' when the debugger paused here, the result of TiDB is exactly the same with MySQL.

The result of `source sql.txt` is different in my local environment this time:
```text
tidb> source sql.txt
ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
tidb> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    415
Current database: test

ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
tidb> source sql.txt
ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away
No connection. Trying to reconnect...
Connection id:    417
Current database: test

ERROR 1153 (08S01): Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes
```

But I exactly also encountered the weird behavior like yours previously. Is it a problem related to mysql client?

I see, it is related to the [`auto-tls`](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/dev/tidb-configuration-file#auto-tls) configuration, if it is set to `true`, the error message is `ERROR 2006 (HY000): MySQL server has gone away`.
